analysis.rationale: R1 re-analysis reproduces R0 signals on all 5 pairs (block_boundary 0.9990-1.0017 << 1.1; unique_G ratios 0.83-0.95 with pair3 clean itself only 233; gm_ratio/anisotropy/glass all Gaussian-sev4-like; noise_prior sigma 0.74-1.85 at estimator floor). Two R0 statements are corrected: (1) the '2.11% clipped whites' is actually DARK clipping (<=1) - decomposed per pair target highlight (>=254) = 0.0% everywhere, dark extremes match blur-only sim almost exactly (2.11/18.00% vs 2.09/17.97%); noise is still rejected because all pre-blur noise sims erase BOTH extreme fractions to ~0%. (2) The intensity-dependent residual flagged by ric=0.20-0.38 on 3/5 pairs (gamma_suspect) is a systematic HIGHLIGHT-SHOULDER tone curve present on all pairs: residual (target - blur4 sim) is ~-0.5 below 128, -1..-4 at 160, -3..-5 at 192, -8..-11 at >=224 levels; a pure linear tone fit would gain +0.5..+2.4 dB (pair0 35.61->38.00). But no x_distortion global function has a mild enough minimum severity (brightness shift +/-25.5 or gamma 0.8/1.4; contrast 0.75/1.4; stretch identity/0.9; saturation 0.7/0.6; quantization 20-24 colors would collapse unique_G 244-><=24), and numeric tests confirm (brightness-gamma 20.34 dB, contrast-scale 25.06 dB). Non-x_distortion blur re-implementations (PIL/cv2/linear-light/JPEG-intermediate q90-98) were also checked and none exceeds 35.5 dB, so the shoulder is a generator-side OOD tone difference that no representable pipeline can remove. Best representable pipeline therefore remains blur_gaussian:4 (UNCERTAIN because pair0 simulation PSNR 35.61 is in the 30-40 band).
